title: C482/1117/2012 of DILIP SINGH SEKHAWAT Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ANR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Recall Application MCRC 346 of 2019
Delay in Recall Application CRMA 3760 of 2019
In
Criminal Misc. Application No. 1117 of 2012
Dilip Singh Shekhawat .......Applicant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & ors. .......Respondents
Mr. Pawan Mishra, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Anchit Khokhar, Advocate for the respondent/recall applicant.
Mr. Sandeep Tandon, Dy. A.G. with Mr. Lalit Miglani, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.(oral)

Instant Recall application alongwith delay
condonation application has been filed by the respondent
no.2/recall applicant seeking recall of the order dated
09.08.2019 and 13.08.2019.
2. There is 70 days' delay in filing the present
recall application. Delay condonation application is
supported by an affidavit, wherein it is stated that the
criminal misc. application was dismissed for want of
prosecution and the interim order was also vacated vide
order dated 14.06.2017 and thereafter the case was
proceeded by the trial Court and non-bailable warrant
were issued against the original applicant. It is also
stated that when the respondent no.2 approached the
trial court, she came to know that the case has been
decided vide order dated 13.08.2019, then, she came to
the High Court and inquired the status of her case
through her present counsel. Thereafter, the present
counsel applied for certified copy of the order sheet as
well as the copy of final order.

2
3. Perusal of the delay condonation application
would reveal that initially the date was not mentioned in
the said application and after filing the same in the Court
it appears that the delay of 70 days has been mentioned.
However, in the affidavit filed in support of the delay
condonation application, the days of delay in filing the
recall application is also blank. The applicant has not
disclosed in the application or in the affidavit filed in
support of the delay condonation application when she
appeared before the trial court and came to know that
the case has been finally decided by this Court vide
judgment dated 13.08.2019. Further no date has been
mentioned when she contacted her counsel. The delay of
70 days in filing the recall application, though has not
been sufficiently explained but since the delay of 70 days
is ordinate, therefore, the delay in filing the recall
application of 70 days is condoned. Delay condonation
application is allowed.
4. Also heard on the recall application.
5. In the affidavit filed in support of recall
application, it is stated that on 12.03.2013, Mr. Deep
Chandra Joshi, Advocate has filed counter affidavit on
behalf of respondent no.2 and applicant was also granted
time to file rejoinder affidavit. It is also stated that the
case was adjourned several times. Thereafter, almost
after a gap of 3 years the matter was again listed on
14.06.2017, on that day, the case was dismissed for want
of prosecution. Thereafter, the counsel for respondent
no.2-recall applicant informed her that the case was
dismissed in default. It is also stated that the applicant
in this matter is an influential man and he has
considerable influence in the higher rank of the Indian
Army. However, the matter of termination is pending

3
before Armed Forces Tribunal, New Delhi and she is
being permitted to continue to reside in official
accommodation. It is further stated that she is not aware
of filing the restoration application by the applicant
because she was not in contact with her counsel. At this
juncture, it would be apt to reproduce relevant paragraph
of the affidavit in support of recall application, which
reads as under:
"12. That on 26.10.2018, the Hon'ble Court for the
very first time directed the applicant to serve fresh notice to
the respondent no.2. That as per the office report in order
sheet of the case it is stated on office report dated
09.04.2019 that "Notice sent to respondent no.2 comeback
unserved with report that respondent no.2 has been
terminated from service".
13. That the matter was again listed on 10.04.2019
wherein the Hon'ble Court again directed the applicant to
take fresh steps within 1 week but as per office report dated
16.05.2019 steps were not taken.
14. That the matter was again listed on 17.05.2019
wherein Hon'be Court granted 3 days' time to take fresh
steps. That the notice was issued but as per office report
dated 27.06.2019 that "Notice sent to respondent no.2
comeback unserved with report of Kotwali Cantt that the
respondent no.2 has been transferred from M.H. Dehradun".
17. That is pertaining to mention that the
deponents/respondent no.2 was still living in her official
residence on the basis of interim protection order granted by
A.F.T., New Delhi. But she never received any
communication regarding the aforesaid restoration
application though this Hon'ble Court as well as her counsel.
The Hon'ble Court have granted several opportunities to
applicant to take notice but the notice to respondent no.2
were never received. That the applicant being an influential
person somehow managed to stop the delivery of notices as
evident from the fact that in one of the office report it is said
that respondent no.2 is terminated from service while in the
other office report it is said that the applicant has been
transferred.
19. That it is very important to mention that the
applicant have made out a case against respondent no.2 on
the basis of suicide case of one Co. S. Mukhopadhayay. That
to make out a cases the applicant was able to obtain a copy
of suicide note, F.I.R. registered against the respondent no.2,
and copy of judgment passed by Hon'ble High Court of
Gujarat. That subsequently the trial in this matter was
conducted which was registered as session case no. 37/2013
"The State of Gujarat Vs. Major Poonam Chaturvedi" wherein
vide order dated 24.11.2014 passed by Sessions Judge,
Kuchchh at Bhuj, the respondent no.2 Poonam Chaturvedi

4
was acquitted. That the acquittal order is very detailed and
categorical.
20. That when the applicant has all the information
about the above said case then they also had the knowledge
of the acquittal of respondent no.2, but instead of presenting
true facts before this Hon'ble High Court, the applicant has
deliberately concealed the material facts and circumstances
and mislead the Hon'ble High Court into believing that the
respondent no.2 gas earlier blackmailed on Col. S.
Mukhopadhyay, who later committed suicide because of
respondent no.2. Therefore, playing fraud upon this Hon'ble
High Court as Hon'ble Hihg Court have relied upon the Col.
S. Mukhopadhyay case while passing the final order on the
wrong facts argued by the applicant. It is a case of bare and
simple fraud practiced upon the Court and it is trite that
fraud vitiates everything.
21. That when the respondent no.2 approached the
Court below to find out the status of her case thereupon she
came to know that the whole case has been quashed by
Hon'ble Court vide order dated 13.08.2019. Thereafter, she
came to Hon'ble HIhg Court of Uttarakhand where she
inquired about the status of her case from her present
consul as she was not in contact with earlier counsel.
Thereafter, the present counsel applied for the certified copy
of order sheet, restoration order and final order.
22. That the order dated 09.08.2019 and
13.08.2019 passed by the Hon'ble the High Court is an ex-parte against respondent no.2, which is contrary to the
Rules of natural justice enshrined in the principal Audi
alteram partem.
23. That the final order has been passed against
respondent no.2 based on wrong facts provided by the
applicant and without affording any opportunity of hearing
causing serious prejudice to her."
6. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that that all the paragraphs have been
verified/swore in personal knowledge of respondent no.2-
recall applicant, namely, Poonam Chaturvedi. He would
further submit that perusal of the averments made in
paragraphs would reveal that the respondent no.2- recall
applicant was aware of the every proceedings of this
Court as well as the order passed by this Court issuing
notice to respondent no.2. Meaning thereby, the
respondent no.2-recall applicant was having knowledge
of the pendency of the recall application and notice
issued to her time to time but she tried to avoid the
service effected upon her, therefore, this Court observed

5
that as the vakalatnama of Mr. Deep Chandra Joshi,
Advocate, which is on record and has not been
withdrawn by him at the time when this Court allowed
the criminal misc. application vide order 13.08.2019. He
would further submit that the vakalatnama of Mr. Deep
Chandra Joshi, Advocate has not been withdrawn as yet,
however, recall application has been filed by the
respondent no.2-recall application by engaging Mr.
Anchit Khokher, Advocate on her behalf.
7. Learned counsel for respondent no.2-recall
applicant would submit that the allegations made in the
recall application that the applicant has obtained the
order dated 13.08.2019 from this Court by suppression
and concealing the material facts. He would further
submit that the applicant mislead this Court into
believing that the respondent no.2-recall applicant has
earlier blackmailed one Col. S. Mukhopadhyay, who later
committed suicide because of respondent no.2-recall
applicant, but he did not provide the copy of judgment
passed by Sessions Judge, Gujarat, in which vide order
dated 24.11.2014, the respondent no.2 was acquitted
from all the charges framed against her but the applicant
has concealed this material fact. However, the order of
acquittal was well within the knowledge of the applicant.
It is contended that since the applicant deliberately
concealed the facts of acquittal of respondent no.2/recall
applicant by the Sessions Judge, Gujarat, therefore, the
applicant not only mislead but also played fraud upon
this Court.
8. To this, learned counsel for the applicant
would submit that the counter affidavit has been filed by
respondent no.2 on 11.03.2013 and thereafter rejoinder
affidavit was filed by the applicant on 27.06.2014,

6
whereof as per the statement of respondent no.2- recall
applicant that the acquittal order was passed on
24.11.2014. Since, the order dated 24.11.2017 acquitting
the respondent no.2-recall applicant was passed by even
after filing of the rejoinder affidavit by the applicant,
thus, it cannot be presumed that the applicant-Dilip
Singh Shekhawat has ever concealed the order of
acquittal of respondent no.2 from this Court.
9. Perusal of the restoration application filed by
learned counsel for the applicant dated 21.11.2017
would reveal that the copy of the restoration application
was served upon Mr. Deep Chandra Joshi, learned
Advocate appearing for the respondent no.2-recall
applicant at that point of time. The restoration
application was listed, counsel for the applicant did not
appear, on precautionary, this Court issued notice to
respondent no.2, it appears to this Court that recall
applicant-respondent no.2 avoid the service effected upon
her. It is settled preposition in law, once a counsel
engaged by party and counsel does not withdraw his/her
vakalatnama filed on behalf of party, the power of lawyer
continues until the vakalatnama is not withdrawn. Since,
the vakalatnama was not withdrawn by the Advocate
appearing on behalf of the respondent no.2-recall
applicant and this Court having considered the aforesaid
settled preposition in law allowing the restoration
application vide order dated 09.08.2019. The relevant
paragraph of the said order is extracted below:
"Restoration application MCRC No. 468 of 2017 along
with delay condonation application CRMA No. 2087 of 2017
has been filed on behalf of the petitioner seeking recall of the
order dated 14.06.2017.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that
Mr. Deep Chandra Joshi, Advocate for respondent no.2 has
refused to accept the copy of the application.
Since, vakalatnama of Mr. Deep Chandra Joshi,
Advocate is on record and has not been withdrawn yet, he

7
shall be deemed to be continue as counsel for respondent
no.2.
Delay of 129 days has sufficiently been explained.
Thus, delay condonation application in filing the restoration
application is allowed. Delay is condoned.
Also, restoration application is allowed. Order dated
14.06.2017 is hereby recalled. C-482 petition is restored to
its original number along with interim order."
10. The present recall application has been filed
inter alia on the grounds that initially when the case was
listed on 12.10.2012, the Court stayed the proceedings
pending before the trial Court and the notices were
issued to respondent no.2. It is also stated that on
12.03.2013, Mr. Deep Chandra Joshi, Advocate appeared
on behalf of respondent no.2 and filed counter affidavit
on her behalf and applicant was also granted three
weeks' time to file rejoinder affidavit. Thereafter, several
times the matter was adjourned. Thereafter, almost after
three years, the matter was again listed on 14.06.2017,
on that day, the case was dismissed for want of
prosecution. Thereafter, Mr. Deep Chandra Joshi,
Advocate has informed the respondent no.2 that the case
was dismissed for want of prosecution and after receiving
the Court's order, the trial begins and, thereafter, non
bailable warrant was issued against the applicant.
11. Perusal of recall application would reveal that
the recall applicant-respondent no.2 made false
statements in the affidavit and tried to mislead this Court
by making false averments in the affidavit filed in support
of the recall application, which appears to this Court, the
same have been made to obtain a favourable order.
12. Learned counsel for the recall applicant-respondent no.2 placed reliance upon the judgment of
Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Jalal-ud-Din Sofi Vs.
State of Jammu and Kashmir and others 2018 SCC

8
Online J & K 519. Paragraph nos. 3 & 4 are extracted
below:
"3. The short and simple grievance of the petitioner
is that the order impugned has been passed at his back and
he has not been given an opportunity of being heard before
the order was passed. To canvass his argument, the learned
counsel for the petitioner has placed explicit reliance on the
law laid MP No. 01/2015 in Page 2 of 3 561-A No. 09/2010
down in the case of State of Punjab v. Davinder Pal Singh
Bhullar & Ors., reported in AIR 2012 Supreme Court 364,
Paragraph Nos. 26 and 27 of which are relevant for the
determination of the matter and these are reproduced
hereinbelow, word for word and letter for letter:
26. There is no power of review with the
Criminal Court after judgment has been rendered. The
High Court can alter or review its judgment before it is
signed. When an order is passed, it cannot be
reviewed. Section 362 Cr. P.C. is based on an
acknowledged principle of law that once a matter is
finally disposed of by a Court, the said Court in the
absence of a specific statutory provision becomes
functus officio and is disentitled to entertain a fresh
prayer for any relief unless the former order of final
disposal is set aside by a Court of competent
jurisdiction in a manner prescribed by law. The Court
becomes functus officio the moment the order for
disposing of a case is signed. Such an order cannot be
altered except to the extent of correcting a clerical or
arithmetical error. There is also no provision for
modification of the judgment. Moreover, the
prohibition contained in Section 362 Cr. P.C. is
absolute; after the judgment is signed, even the High
Court in exercise of its inherent power under Section
482 Cr. P.C. has no authority or jurisdiction to
alter/review the same.
27. If a judgment has been pronounced without
jurisdiction or in violation of principles of natural
justice or where the order has been pronounced
without giving an opportunity of being heard to a party
affected by it or where an order was obtained by abuse
of the process of court which would really amount to
its being without jurisdiction, inherent powers can be
exercised to recall such order for the reason that in
such an eventuality the order becomes a nullity and
the provisions of Section 362 Cr. P.C. would not
operate. In such eventuality, the judgment is
manifestly contrary to the audi alteram partem rule of
natural justice. The power of recall is different from
the power of altering/reviewing the judgment.
However, the party seeking recall/alteration has to
establish that it was not at fault.
4. Applying the ratio of the law laid down above to the
facts of the instant case, the criminal Court does not have
the power to review the judgment after the date of its
delivery. The High Court has the power to alter or review its
judgment before it is signed, but once the order is passed, it
cannot be subjected to review. The Court becomes functus

9
officio the moment the order for disposing of a case is signed
and such an order can only be altered to the extent of
correcting a clerical or arithmetical error. The law laid down
above provides if further that if the High Court in exercise of
its inherent power under Section 482 Cr. P.C. (which
corresponds to Section 561-A Cr. P.C. applicable to the State
of Jammu & Kashmir), has no authority or jurisdiction to
alter/ review the MP No. 01/2015 in Page 3 of 3 561-A No.
09/2010 same. However, para 27 cited above carves out the
exceptions, under the shade and cover of which the High
Court can, in exercise of its inherent powers, recall an order.
It envisions four situations under which such a power can be
exercised that are, first, if the judgment is pronounced
without jurisdiction; second, if it is in violation of the
principles of natural justice; third, if it has been pronounced
without giving an opportunity of being heard to the party
affected by it; and fourth, where the order is obtained by
abuse of the process of the Court. The judicial precedent
evolved above further stipulates that if an order which falls
within the four conditions as stated and enumerated above,
the same is manifestly contrary to the audi alteram partem
rule of natural justice and this power of recall is different
from the power of altering/ reviewing the judgment. In the
case on hand, the petition of the petitioner is squarely
covered under the two situations, that are that the order has
been passed behind the back of the petitioner and he has
not been given an opportunity of being heard."
13. Learned counsel for the recall applicant-respondent no.2 placed reliance upon the judgment of
Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Union of India Vs. K.M.
Shankarappa passed in Civil Appeal No. 3106 of 1991
decided on 28.11.2000. Paragraph no. 7 is extracted
below:
"7.We are unable to accept the submission of the
learned counsel. The Government has chosen to establish a
quasi- judicial body which has been given the powers, inter
alia, to decide the effect of the film on the public. Once a
quasi-judicial body like the Appellate Tribunal, consisting of
a retired Judge of a High Court or a person qualified to be a
Judge of a High Court and other experts in the filed, gives its
decision that decision would be final and binding so far as
the Executive and the Government is concerned. To permit
the Executive to review and/or revise that decision would
amount to interference with the exercise of judicial functions
by a quasi-judicial Board. It would amount to subjecting the
decision of a quasi-judicial body to the scrutiny of the
Executive. Under our Constitution the position is reverse.
The Executive has to obey judicial orders. Thus, Section
6(1) is a travesty of the rule of law which is one of the basic
structures of the Constitution. The Legislature may, in
certain cases, overrule or nullify the judicial or executive

10
decision by enacting an appropriate legislation. However,
without enacting an appropriate legislation, the Executive or
the Legislature cannot set at naught a judicial order. The
Executive cannot sit in an appeal or review or revise a
judicial order. The Appellate Tribunal consisting of experts
and decides matters quasi-judicially. A Secretary and/or
Minister cannot sit in appeal or revision over those decisions.
At the highest, the Government may apply to the Tribunal
itself for a review, if circumstances so warrant. But the
Government would be bound by the ultimate decision of the
Tribunal."
14. Having gone through the judgments (Supra),
this Court is of the view that this Court has not decided
the case without affording opportunity of hearing to the
respondent no.2. Rather notices were issued to her and
she also engaged the lawyer who filed the counter
affidavit on her behalf but subsequently she did not
appear to contest the case, therefore, the ratio of the
judgments (Supra) is not applicable on the facts and
circumstances of the present case and judgment (Supra)
have no help to the respondent no.2-recall applicant in
any manner. Since no sufficient reason is made out to
recall the order dated 13.08.2019. The application is
misconceived. Same is liable to be dismissed and same is
hereby dismissed.
15. Since, respondent no.2/recall applicant has
tried to mislead this Court by filing a false affidavit and
now a days, it appears that the litigant are not afraid in
filing the false affidavit before the Court. The applicant-respondent no.2 has not come before the Court with
clean hands and has filed the recall application on false
and frivolous ground. The conduct of a person is a
relevant factor. A person, who has not come with clean
hands and has suppressed the material facts, does not
deserve any relief from the Court and exemplary cost
should be imposed upon him for wasting valuable time of
the Court. I, being a member of Division Bench, while

11
relying upon the case of Suraz India Trust v. Union of
India reported in (2017) 14 SCC 416, delivered a
judgment dated 26.10.2018 in the case of Sunita Pandey
& another vs. State of Uttarakhand & Ors. [WPPIL
No.132 of 2014], thereby dismissing the Public Interest
Litigation with costs of Rs.50,000/- upon the petitioners
for filing false and frivolous petition.
16. In the present case, the delay condonation
application has been filed on false grounds, this Court is
of the view that stern action should be taken against
such litigant to mislead this Court. In view of the above,
this Court is of the view that the recall application should
be dismissed with the costs of Rs. 50,000/- to be paid by
the recall applicant/respondent no.2.
17. After the aforesaid order was dictated, the
learned Counsel for the recall applicant/respondent no.2
submitted that he is a new counsel and imposition of
cost is certainly ruin his carrier. He would submit that he
will not repeat the conduct and tendered unconditional
apology and prayed that the cost imposed upon recall
applicant/respondent no.2 be waived.
18. In view of the foregoing discussion, the recall
application is dismissed. Though this Court think that
the recall applicant/respondent no.2 is liable to pay the
cost of Rs. 50,000/- for filing recall application on
frivolous grounds but having accepted the unconditional
apology of learned counsel for the recall
applicant/respondent no.2, this Court waives the
imposition of cost upon him.
 (Lok Pal Singh,J.)
Mamta 13.12.2019
